ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.5–2 meters. It features a copper-brown head with three distinct black streaks radiating from the eyes and a body patterned with dark-edged, pale-centered crossbands.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Coelognathus radiatus* is the presence of three distinct black streaks radiating from the eye: one upward, one backward, and one downward.
ai.habitat: *Coelognathus radiatus* inhabits diverse environments, ranging from tropical deciduous forests and scrublands to agricultural fields, typically at elevations below 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Copper-head Trinket Snake often performs a dramatic defensive display by flattening its neck and body to appear larger while striking repeatedly.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Coelognathus radiatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the warmer months, often peaking between April and June in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Coelognathus radiatus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the Himalayan foothills and plains, ranging from sea level to approximately 1,500 meters elevation.
